title: The Copper Lattice — Editor Intro
summary: Opening splash reframes the Esperanza success as a capacity problem: one relay can prove access, but a durable network must make help travel farther than the machine carrying it.
panelPlan: Full-page opening/title splash. The Launch-Shop command table is overwhelmed by incoming community requests while one small fading orbital symbol sits alone above a broad Mojave map.
Use scale and negative space: many destinations below, one fragile path above. The crew can appear as partial working silhouettes but should not be staged explaining anything.
Do not show legacy relay sites, timing modules, ground nodes, copper hardware or the eventual lattice. The page asks the problem; the issue earns the solution.
Set the captions in clean editorial blocks that tighten around the single-word line ONE and then open into the issue title.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: One impossible night became seven requests before breakfast.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The relay that saved Esperanza can reach one more town before its orbit becomes useless.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Launch-Shop can keep solving the same emergency one town at a time.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Or they can solve a different problem:

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: how to make help travel farther than the machine carrying it.

directionInline.text: Non-diegetic opening title page. Preserve exact caption text. It should remind the reader what is loaded after Issue 1 and create appetite for the scale problem, without revealing how Issue 2 solves it. No ground-relay design, timing-module salvage, routing architecture, seizure or later network outcome.
